body.translated_text: (1.1-2) On the lovely peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, attended by <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Cāraṇas</s>, thronged with <s>Siddha</s>-yogins, endowed with various trees, teeming with hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>, attended by <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>, pervaded by various [beings], variegated with diverse minerals, (1.3-4) strewn with many peaks, attended by <s>Gaṇas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s>, possessing the splendor of heated gold with a thousand rays, frequented by sages, attended by hosts of <s>Siddhas</s>, amidst a forest of <s>karṇikāra</s> trees, with blooming <s>campaka</s> flowers and the like, (1.5-6) adorned with <s>sarja</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, and <s>kadamba</s> trees, with <s>pāṭalī</s> and <s>aśoka</s> — there, on that lovely mountain, He dwelt together with <s>Umā</s>, upon a wondrous seat studded with gems, made of gold, (1.6-7) the God wearing a garland of skulls, five-faced and attended, endowed with sixteen arms, with [beautiful] eyes, his matted locks bound up in an elevated crown, with the crescent moon as his crest-ornament, (1.8-9) with tawny hair, supremely terrifying, blazing like fire, wearing a serpent as his sacred thread, with great <s>ghoṇa</s>-earrings, adorned with bracelets, serpent-king armlets, and waist-cords, (1.9-10) He, the Lord of gods, shines — bearer of half the body of <s>Umā</s>, holding a sword and a club, the God with a trident in hand, fearsome, a hero bearing [a great weapon], likewise holding a thunderbolt and a blade, (1.11-12) with a spear and an axe in hand, adorned with a rosary, with the lotus-hands [filled] with a great corpse, made into ear-ornaments, wearing an elephant-hide as an upper garment, fearsome with a bell in hand, wearing a tiger-skin as a lower garment, difficult to behold even for the gods, (1.13-14) with sunken eyes, bearing great weapons, adorned with great <s>mudrās</s>, with a great lolling tongue, the creator of <s>saṃsāra</s> and emanation, holding a skull in his left hand and a <s>ḍamaru</s> (drum) in [another] hand, with a discus, a bow, and arrows in hand as well, (1.15-16) holding a [lotus?] and also <s>Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (the Goddess) in hand, laughing and shrieking, supremely terrifying with loud laughter — having assumed the <s>Bhairava</s> form, surrounded by great yogins. Thus in bliss...

As the foolish [do not understand] the true nature of the scriptures, nor the bliss of a maiden-woman, so the most sinful man turns away from the <s>Kaulika</s> [path]. Thus, those deluded by ignorance, bewildered by the net of scriptures, do not know the supreme bliss, the supreme nectar of <s>Kula</s>-knowledge.
[This] grants attainment as one wishes, O Goddess, presided over by the power of will (<s>Icchāśakti</s>). In whatever guise, by whatever observance, where there is no [distinction of] various practices, duality or non-duality, according to desire — at the [appropriate] occasion, whenever I [manifest], then I, like an oblation, whether a householder or a celibate student, or in whatever form — of one living as he wishes, stationed here or there — even so, O Queen of Gods, the greatest treasure [received] from the <s>guru</s> — through the possession (<s>samāveśa</s>) of <s>Rudra</s>'s power, [one] attains perfection by <s>Kaula</s> yoga.

body.translated_text: (3.1) He who in the world proclaims the meaning of texts but himself acts otherwise — [such] scholars, puffed up with learning, have gone to a bad destination. (3.2) Satisfied with the literal meaning of syllables, contemplating the meaning of <s>Veda</s>s and scriptures, deluded, a scholar of [mere] meaning does not find the supreme peace. (3.3) [...lacuna...] whence [could there be] knowledge, even by hundreds of tens of millions of texts? Camphor, saffron, and the like — for a donkey-carrier, [they are] useless. (3.4) And many, deceived by incomplete [systems of] discipline (<s>vinaya</s>), cast aside, do not find the bliss of the <s>Kaula</s>, O lovely-faced one! (3.5) Satisfied with <s>mantra</s>s and <s>tantra</s>s, having tasted only a little — not attaining <s>Kaulika</s> knowledge, men are content with [mere] discipline. (3.6–7) White, yellow, and other [...] pungent and the rest; earrings, circular in shape, and also [rites of] kindling; such and other [practices], and also <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (element-purification); <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and <s>Śakti</s>, and the subtle inner path as well. (3.8) Having known the procedure of the knowledge-principles, <s>Śaiva</s>s of satisfied minds — all [should embrace] the <s>Kaulika</s> congregation of <s>Yoginī</s>s, O great souls! (3.9) The <s>Vaineya</s> practitioners are worms, declared to be in the state of bound souls (<s>paśu</s>) — [the comparison is] of gold and clay, of elephant and mosquito. (3.10) Such is the distinction, O Goddess, between the <s>Kaula</s> and the <s>Vaineya</s> — [...lacuna...] as an elephant [among lesser creatures]. (3.11) So shines the Lord of <s>Kaula</s>s, wandering upon the earth's surface, endowed with colored syllables, furnished with the syllables of <s>Kaula</s> knowledge. (3.12) The wish-fulfilling jewel of meditation, the yoga of the inconceivable — [text breaks off]

body.translated_text: (4.2) She, O Goddess, is all-pervading, [dwelling] in the hearts of all embodied beings; awakened by the jewel of the instruction of knowledge (<s>jñānopadeśa</s>), one becomes enlightened. (4.3) He who, in the form of the all-pervader, is beheld [as the unity of] <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> — this <s>Rudraśakti</s>, O Goddess, abides in the mouth of the <s>āveśa</s>-guru (the guru of possession). (4.4) He whom they call the unthinkable, <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause — from that Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) has issued forth the <s>Śakti</s> (power), which differentiates into <s>nāda</s> (sound) and <s>bindu</s> (point). (4.5) By the mere utterance of that [mantra], conviction (<s>pratyaya</s>) arises; and from that, the mass of <s>karma</s> is obstructed. (4.6) Through practice, the divine [power] is present — the divine, O Goddess, is situated in the body; within three months, O Goddess, the vision of the <s>yoginī</s>s [and their] breaking-through [is attained]. (4.7) One sees the divine gods and [their] celestial palaces (<s>vimāna</s>s), O beautiful-faced one; according to [the degree of] one's practice, O Goddess, creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) proceeds. (4.8) First the heart trembles, and there is utterance from the palate; the head too whirls — that is the sign of the transmission of creation (<s>sṛṣṭisaṃkrānti</s>). (4.9) One should cause each [limb] to whirl, in the joints of the limbs and sub-limbs; this entire body is made to whirl by the power of <s>Kaulavidyā</s> (the Kaula knowledge). (4.10) ...transformations; the states [of consciousness], with desire, make [various conditions]; in each of those, one should not be afraid — the Supreme Goddess (<s>Parameśvarī</s>) is playing. (4.11) There are no demons (<s>bhūta</s>s) or goblins (<s>piśāca</s>s), nor is one afflicted by delusion; nor is there...obstruction...and suffering is released. (4.12) In the form of <s>icchāśakti</s> (the power of will), she becomes the guru of the yogin — producing the bliss of love (<s>ratyānanda</s>) in the body, the supreme [power] that removes all sins. (4.13) Sons, friends...wealth and... what is desired and undesired depart [becoming equal] for one whose mind has tasted <s>yoga</s>. (4.14) One sees the divine gods established in celestial palaces, O beautiful-faced one; the possession (<s>āveśa</s>) produced by <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>...the unconscious [state]. (4.15) The possession by <s>Rudraśakti</s> (<s>rudraśaktisamāveśa</s>) — the eternal possession [that is] beyond consciousness — through union with the divine gods, is the cause of supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda</s>). (4.16) [Arising] from the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>)...granting the fruits of enjoyment (<s>bhukti</s>) and liberation (<s>mukti</s>); the possession by <s>Rudraśakti</s> arises in sound and vision. (4.17) The one yoked in <s>yoga</s> does not know day or night, O beautiful-faced one; they do not know hunger or thirst; there is no bodily suffering for that one. (4.18) There arise delight and contentment, and ever-constant bliss; endowed with consciousness, one performs various <s>mudrā</s>-bindings (<s>mudrābandha</s>s). (4.19) Trembling, singing, dancing, and transformations of many kinds — one performs [these] by the transformation of impurity (<s>mala</s>), spontaneously arising among many [practitioners]. (4.20) One shakes off impurity...the supreme <s>Śakti</s> situated in the body; what is spoken untruly does not come to pass. (4.21) One does not see the signs of <s>yoga</s>, nor has the <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) been traversed anywhere; but if it has been traversed, then one certainly sees [the truth]. (4.22) Otherwise, even in tens of millions of scriptures (<s>śāstra</s>s), one who knows thus does not proceed [further].

Thus ends the fourth chapter of the <s>Timirodghāṭana</s>.

[<s>Kaula</s> knowledge instruction and its rewards]

<s>Bhairava</s> spoke:

(5.1-2) Hear, O Goddess, from below to above, the instruction in <s>Kaula</s> knowledge, obtained from the teaching of the <s>Guru</s>, bestowing the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. When knowledge has been transmitted, then liberation is assured; like a potter's wheel, O Goddess, the cage of the body revolves. (5.3) [Through...] beings, the power of knowledge not yet manifested — they enjoy various pleasures, bestowing the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. (5.4-5) Attraction, subjugation, creating enmity, expulsion, and killing, and also royal honor, stupefaction, immobilization, and the like — it produces conviction in this, and the power of speech in many ways; and whatever <s>vidyās</s> (spells) are taught in <s>mantras</s> and <s>tantras</s>, these too it grants. (5.6-7) Perfected in all rites, bestowing the fruits of all actions, the supreme of all <s>tantras</s>, differentiated for all classes: the auspicious one that revives the dead; red-orange for stupefaction and attraction; (5.7-8) yellow with smoke-colored radiance for immobilization, prescribed for expulsion; black, causing death to enemies; blood-red in battle; lotus-hued, she shines with glory, [and white?] with the radiance of beauty. (5.9-10) <s>Aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), and <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), and <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will) and the <s>Śiva</s>-principle, <s>vaśitva</s> (mastery), and wherever there is desire — hearing and beholding with reverence, the eighth has been declared. Through the power of <s>Kaula</s> knowledge, the eightfold sovereignty arises. (5.11-12) That by which qualities are produced — that beloved [teaching] I shall declare: twelve verses, taught as the vision of all. It must be carefully guarded; one should not have it written by a scribe. (5.12-13) These twelve verses, O beautiful-faced one, within seven days — it should not be given to the unlearned; it should be transmitted from ear to ear. Having obtained that, <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) occurs — the emission is the unity of creation. (5.14-15) At that very instant, the <s>mudrā</s> called <s>Khecarī</s> (space-moving) is bound, without doubt. One seed-syllable, filled with creation; one <s>mudrā</s>, the <s>Khecarī</s>. He by whom these two are known — he too abides in the state of peace. (5.15-16) The yogin established in that state beholds even the three worlds; they arise in an instant; knowledge of the three times would come about.

body.translated_text: (6.1) What is that <s>śakti</s> (power) that transmigrates? What signs does it show? What disturbances and transformations does it produce, established in the body? (6.2) How is the transmitted [<s>śakti</s>] to be recognized? What is done when it has transmigrated? How does the ascending jewel [of <s>śakti</s>] move downward and upward? (6.3) ...how is [it] to be recognized? In what time does it grant <s>siddhi</s> (attainment)? What are the signs of one who has attained <s>siddhi</s>? Tell this, O <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord). <s>Bhairava</s> spoke: (6.4) That [<s>śakti</s>] which, in the form of the all-pervading, in the <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg) with its moving and unmoving [beings], (6.5) having pervaded downward and upward — she is remembered as all-pervading. Established both externally and internally in the body, abiding in all living beings, (6.6) by the instruction of a true teacher (<s>sadācārya</s>), she transmigrates into another's body. Movement and rest, downward and upward — that is the characteristic of bodily transmigration. (6.7) Downward is the transmigration of withdrawal (<s>saṃhāra</s>); upward is emanation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), O fair-faced one. With movement, rest, and stability — the threefold <s>yoga</s> proceeds. (6.8) Thus, by stages, one should pierce; by the three, [the teacher] should instruct in each one. The supreme <s>śakti</s>, pervading the body downward and upward, should be made to enter. (6.9) One in whom these signs [are present] — he is remembered as a liberation-granting teacher (<s>gurur mokṣadaḥ</s>). Having performed all services with one's own self or with wealth, (6.10) that supreme knowledge, situated in the mouth of the teacher, should be grasped. By the jewel of <s>Kaula</s> instruction, the yogin [gains] divine vision: (6.11) he sees [the <s>yoginī</s>] with closed eyes, and again through direct perception. The <s>yoginī</s> [appears] at first as a mere shadow, again and again; (6.12) as one practices the <s>yoga</s>, so does the form manifest. [One] sees her in dark form — wrathful or in gentle form, adorned with various ornaments. (6.13) Appearing and disappearing, she stands and is seen in many forms. Abiding always in the sky, all [practitioners] behold the Mother — (6.14) in wrathful and terrifying form, surrounded by many <s>yoginī</s>s. And the city of the Lord of yogins (<s>yogeśvara</s>) — he himself beholds it in bliss (<s>ātmānanda</s>). (6.15) The <s>Kaulika</s> [teaching], obtained through the jewel of <s>yoga</s>, O fair-faced one — there is no substance on earth which, if given, would discharge [that] debt. (6.16) To one who gives the <s>Kaula</s> instruction, the rare liberation-granting teacher, who would cut through <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) — to him one should give [everything], with nothing held back. (6.17) The divine nectar of <s>Kaula</s> knowledge, established in many divisions — I have told only a little of it; it is seen in tens of millions of divisions. (6.18) In twenty-seven years is told the <s>Siddhakhecarī</s> [practice]. The lord of yogins who is always engaged [in practice] — he quickly attains <s>siddhi</s>. (6.19) Thus all has been declared by me, that which you asked, O beloved.

body.translated_text: (7.2) The lord of yogins, constantly engaged, sees the entire three worlds; he sees the cosmic egg as penetrated — beyond that, he goes to <s>Śiva</s>. (7.3) First he perceives forms at the end of dream-sleep, with eyes closed; through constant practice of yoga, [he attains] direct vision of the gods. (7.4) He hears their speech as well, and [perceives] touch and even smell; the lord of yogins, mighty in power, his mind established in truth, (7.5) displays a divine form to all the world in the sky; the wise one causes wonders thus, and accomplishes whatever he wishes. (7.6) Endowed with the meaning of scriptures and united with <s>Vedānta</s>, he composes elegant <s>kāvya</s> (poetry), charming with ornamental figures. (7.7) They agitate the entire world, imbued with enchanting practices, possessing men and women, and [producing] captivating songs. (7.8) The yogin, established in divine yoga, sees through elevation of mind — (7.9) in <s>Pātāla</s> (the netherworld) and the world of <s>Nāgas</s>, the divine three worlds, wondrous human realms, grasses, shrubs, and creepers, (7.10) bipeds and quadrupeds and aquatic creatures of many kinds, beautiful territories and regions, villages and cities; (7.11) he shows wondrous syllables in the sky, oceans between continents, pleasure-gardens and mountains, (7.12) <s>Yakṣiṇīs</s> of various forms, and [...] especially; he sees the celestial chariots of the moon and sun and the world of <s>Indra</s>, (7.13) the lovely guardian-cities of the directions, and the cities of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> likewise; the divine, human, and netherworld [realms] — he who sets their activities in motion, (7.14) the supreme <s>Śakti</s> shows the three worlds with their moving and unmoving [beings], together with <s>Rudra</s>'s city, the auspicious five-faced city [of <s>Śiva</s>]. (7.15) That supreme [realm] of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, presided over by the supreme <s>Śakti</s> — above that, <s>Śiva</s> [abides], peaceful, established without interruption. (7.16) Having pierced the cosmic egg through <s>śakti</s>, he goes to the supreme [state]; [... corrupt ...] he attains liberation and release. (7.17) This has been told to you, O Goddess, in proper sequence, from highest to lowest; O Goddess, one who is established in <s>Kaula</s> yoga quickly goes to the peaceful state.

body.translated_text: (8.2) In the descent of <s>Kaula</s> emanation, the characteristic meaning of the supreme text — the instruction in <s>Rudraśakti</s> (the power of <s>Rudra</s>) is obtained from the mouths of teachers. (8.4) It is the heart of all <s>vidyās</s> (sacred knowledge), remembered as the supreme power of <s>mantras</s>; he who does not know the <s>Rudraśaktisamāveśa</s> (descent of <s>Rudra</s>'s power) does not attain perfection. (8.5) The <s>Kaulika</s> knowledge that cannot be written is established in the mouths of teachers; it should be transmitted from ear to ear — one who stands afar should not transmit it. (8.6) <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), and the instruction in the <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) of yoga — the five jewels of instruction should be written according to the meaning of the text. (8.7) When the first jewel is attained, through practice, grey hair is destroyed; when [the inner fire] blazes upward in the body, one reaches the supreme state. (8.8) By the power of the second jewel, the teacher is gratified by the disciple; honored by the circle of <s>yoginīs</s>, they are established here and there. (8.9) At the third, [there is] the body of another — the transmigration of <s>śakti</s> into one's own body; all those before are agitated — the great-powered one established in <s>samādhi</s>.

body.translated_text: (9.1) How did the supreme <s>Śakti</s> (<s>Parāśakti</s>) originate? How does she pervade the three worlds? All yogins meditate [upon her], the bestower of the path to liberation. <s>Bhairava</s> spoke: (9.2) She consists of all gods, O Goddess, established above all worlds, all-pervading and without beginning, worshiped among all gods. (9.3) Having pervaded the fourteen worlds, established above the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), [she is the unity of] <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>... [she is] worshiped in all [forms]. (9.4) Seated in the lotus posture (<s>padmāsana</s>), with a rosary and a water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>), wearing matted locks and bark-garments — thus is the worship of <s>Brahmā</s>... (9.5) ...one worships through <s>yoga</s>; bearing conch, discus, and club — thus is <s>Viṣṇu</s> worshiped. (9.6) From that [Śakti], bearing the ash-smeared <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff), blazing with skull-ornaments, in naked form, bearing [various attributes] — I myself [am worshiped thus], O beautiful-eyed one. (9.7) What indeed does [one] see, O fair-eared one? With the mind always fixed upon the eternal [Śakti], <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s> meditate upon the supreme <s>Śakti</s>. (9.8) And all the other sages too, together with gods, <s>Asura</s>s, and yogins — <s>Indra</s>, <s>Candra</s> (the moon), <s>Sūrya</s> (the sun), and others — all meditate upon the supreme <s>Kalā</s> (creative phase). (9.9) What indeed, O Goddess, was asked long ago by the mighty demons (<s>Dānava</s>s)? ...All the demons came seeking refuge in me. (9.10) By me too was <s>Śakti</s> meditated upon, and likewise by all the gods; she came at that very instant — the supreme <s>Śakti</s>, through my mind. (9.11) ...endowed with [power]...see...they have arrived; by her, all this is pervaded — the three worlds with [their] moving and unmoving [beings]. (9.12) Of that [Śakti]...established...hundreds of thousands of <s>Yoginī</s>s, in many tens of millions. (9.13) Even as one, she abides in many forms, pervading [all], having attained the supreme state; and [there is] another, and yet another <s>Śakti</s>... (9.14) She, though one, is divided into three aspects, established in many divisions. The first, the highest, [arising] by your grace, is of great power from the moment of [her] birth. (9.15) The second, the middle <s>Śakti</s>, is situated in the mouths of <s>Yoginī</s>s; [she bestows] knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), and instruction in the <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) of <s>yoga</s>. (9.16) She causes the transmission of knowledge through the possession by <s>Rudraśakti</s> (<s>rudraśaktisamāveśa</s>); ...this is declared to be the characteristic of the middle <s>Śakti</s>. (9.17) Through the instruction of the <s>guru</s>, perfection (<s>saṃsiddhi</s>) [is attained]; through practice, the state that grants liberation. In the thirty-two <s>mātṛcakra</s>s (circles of the mothers), the third <s>Śakti</s>... (9.18) ...may one perform with <s>mantra</s>, [but only] after some time, always; these qualities do not arise — [she is the one] granting liberation through divine vision. (9.19) The third <s>Śakti</s>, [associated with] peace...has been declared... having descended through the path of truth, she has entered the families of <s>yoginī</s>s. (9.20) The jewel of blissful instruction — by that, one is known as a bestower of <s>Kaula</s> [knowledge]. Having abandoned the net of [abstract] principles (<s>tattva</s>s), [one grasps] the <s>Kaulika</s> meaning through the <s>tantra</s>. (9.21) ...for the purpose of <s>siddhi</s>, the true <s>guru</s> (<s>sadguru</s>) [bestows] immediate conviction. Rare is the true <s>guru</s>, O Goddess; rare and exceedingly great [is such a one]. (9.22) Rare is the attainment of that very [guru]; [rare is] one who has attained liberation... Therefore, even with great effort, [such a guru] is rare even at the <s>Kaula</s> seat (<s>pīṭha</s>). (9.23) Having gone to many countries, one may wander through [sacred] seats and fields (<s>kṣetrapīṭha</s>s); for twelve years... one does not see [the true guru] at all. (9.24) Even one who is well-educated, O Goddess of gods, a scholar versed in the meaning of many texts — he may wander from seat to seat and return without having accomplished his purpose. (9.25) [Conversely,] even an uneducated fool, devoid of the meaning of all texts — having obtained the <s>Kaula</s> seed-syllable, [attains] <s>siddhi</s> that illuminates the three worlds. (9.26) Thus, this supreme <s>Kaula</s> <s>yoga</s>, the highest of all <s>tantra</s>s — ...granting liberation, O Goddess — it must be concealed again and again.

body.translated_text: (10.11cd) Free from attachment to intoxication and snakebite, desireless, having abandoned greed. (10.12) Observing all fasts and restraints, self-controlled, beloved [...]; properly [following] the [...] vow, virtuous, a keeper of the observance. (10.13) Pacifying [hostile] planetary influences, heroic, pure of soul, a worshiper of the <s>guru</s>; of good character, peaceful, eloquent — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, not of the lowest class. (10.14) [One who knows] the three times — past and future — should not give [the teaching] to the [unworthy] five. To well-examined disciples, in secret, firmly, and for their benefit — (10.15) to those [qualified] by these [qualities], among [all] classes, one should transmit [the teaching]. One who regards wealth, for the sake of the <s>guru</s>, as [worthless as] straw — [even] wife, sons, and the like — (10.16) a disciple who conducts himself thus and offers his entire self — to these [alone], the supreme <s>tattva</s> (reality) [should be given], [the teaching that leads to] equal [vision] in all directions. (10.17) For the sake of your love, [this] has been declared by me. It should not be given to the unexamined [disciple]. The self is corrupted in many ways [...] the meaning of the supreme reality... (10.18) Whether by wealth, by means of illusion (?), or again by service and <s>dharma</s> — [those who] make offerings of the <s>tattva</s> [merely formally] — the reality itself does not approve [of them]. (10.19) [...] producing self-conviction — he who, with concentrated mind, meditates for twelve [months] without laziness — (10.20) endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the other [supernatural powers], omniscience arises. For a three-faced [image], by five <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s; for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, in six, seven, or eight [years]; (10.21) in ten or twelve years [for the others] — [the teaching] should be given [even] at filthy and impure places. It should not be given to the unexamined, nor to a reviler or nihilist. (10.22) One should not practice deceptions; it should not be given to just anyone. [But] if the <s>guru</s> is satisfied with even an inept disciple — (10.23) the prescribed time for him is not to be stated; he should pierce [his ignorance] immediately. A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> may be a deceiver, and a <s>mleccha</s> (barbarian) too may not be a deceiver. (10.24) Even to a <s>mleccha</s> it should be given; one should not give [...] deceptively. The <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), equal to <s>Śiva</s>, bestows grace in the world. (10.25) When greed for wealth has been reached, [the teaching should] not [be given] to kinsmen and relatives [for that reason]. He who [...] the <s>guru</s> [...] will [attain] union. (10.26) Teaching and exposition — awakening the <s>guru</s>-disciple [relationship]; one should worship [the <s>guru</s>] thus, it should be known; having observed for a long time, the <s>guru</s> (10.27) should instruct [...] and should worship the <s>guru</s> accordingly. This [teaching of] the transmigration into another [body], O Goddess, should not be given openly, O beloved. (10.28) For the sake of wealth, even a little sin [is incurred], [by giving] to an unworthy disciple, O virtuous one; otherwise [...] the secret text perishes. (10.29) Therefore it should not be given nor proclaimed — the essence-text that grants liberation.

body.translated_text: (11.2) Previously, yoga was declared by me as sixfold with six limbs, O beloved, with manifold distinctions in meditation, <s>mantra</s>, and other practices. (11.3) Superior to the yoga of [mere] ritual actions, O Goddess, one should contemplate the nectar-yoga (<s>amṛtayoga</s>): whether going, standing, or also [sitting], whether waking or sleeping — (11.4) for one engaged in devoted activity, the eternal yoga proceeds. The mind may be directed elsewhere, the gaze may fall elsewhere — (11.5) yet for the yogin, yoga proceeds uninterrupted. There is neither <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) nor piercing, nor invocation or dismissal. (11.6) In all states, even while playing, for the yogin — by his will he dwells in the forest, by his will in a crowded multitude. (11.7) By his will he enjoys pleasures, by his will he performs vows. This yoga is free from torment, devoid of all [prescribed] actions. (11.8) There is nothing higher than this, O Goddess — supreme delight of the mind; devoid of the syllables of <s>tantra</s> and <s>vidyā</s>, free from <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), (11.9) free from thought, secret, the supremely subtle nectar — the highest. Thus, from the nectar of yoga, O Goddess, the <s>Kaulika</s> [attainment] is obtained [...]. (11.10) Those devoted to the nectar-<s>samādhi</s> — through practice, liberation is attained. Practice is the supreme yoga; the touch of <s>samādhi</s> comes about. (11.11-12) The stainless one sees [...]; in the shape of a <s>kadamba</s> flower-ball, with splendor equal to ten million suns, one beholds it established in the middle of the body — through the stainless [vision] of the yogin. (11.12cd-13) With [...] letters of [...] color, or [like] a trident with the radiance of beauty — one beholds it established in the middle of the body through divine yoga, the yogin. (11.13cd-14) One should see it pervading the entire body, [...] pervading the cosmic egg and all worlds, the Self pervading all downward and upward. (11.14cd-15) The single <s>Kaulika</s> expanse — the [scope] of divine yoga, O virtuous one — this is not seen elsewhere, in all yoga-<s>samādhi</s>s. (11.15cd-16) When told, it is incredible — what wonder and amazement! He to whom the divine Self everywhere experiences conviction, (11.16cd-17) the knowledge dear to those deluded by existence — as long as it is direct perception in the Self; when seen in direct perception, the knowledge born of delusion is destroyed. (11.17cd-18) Thus one sees in direct perception the <s>Rudraśakti</s>, O beloved of the <s>Guru</s>. That which has been taught in the divine yogas — it succeeds not otherwise, O beloved. (11.18cd-19) Having obtained a <s>guru</s> devoid of <s>śakti</s>, whence could a disciple's perfection [come], O beloved? When the root is destroyed, O Goddess, whence [could there be] flowers and fruits? (11.19cd-20) The <s>Rudraśaktisamāveśa</s> (descent of <s>Rudra</s>'s power) — the <s>guru</s> is the supremely weighty, the highest. One whose Self is known, endowed with that — he is the <s>guru</s>, the state granting liberation. (11.20cd-21) In the next world or in all [worlds], having come, [he is] again the liberator. The <s>Kaula</s> [path] is direct-perception conviction — in this world and the next. (11.21cd-22) He who through conviction in this world would also accomplish the next — without conviction in this world, how could there be [conviction] in the beyond? (11.22cd-23) Thus, when [...] knowledge becomes direct perception, one should know the Self from the <s>guru</s> through the threefold inner self. (11.23cd-24) [...lacuna...] the <s>guru</s> [...] that rise and fall [...]. The <s>guru</s> is to be worshiped [...] if one desires one's own perfection. (11.24cd-25) The giver of divine instruction, the teacher-god who is difficult to obtain — where there are many <s>gurus</s>, [there are] empty words without conviction. (11.25cd-26) [...], devoid of valid means, some yogins strike at vital points; some, puffed up by [...] gestures, are arrogant and devoid of knowledge; (11.26cd-27) some are satisfied with [mere] <s>mantras</s>, of little [...]; from the lowest to the highest, [...] at the beginning, some give [teachings as] <s>guru</s>, O Goddess — [but only one who] cuts through <s>saṃsāra</s> [...]. (11.28) [...lacuna...] how could liberation come about? In passion, hatred, and ego — both hate each other mutually. (11.29) Whence could there be the true essence of <s>Kaulika</s> knowledge for them, O beautiful-faced one? [...lacuna...] those incapable, united with others, (11.30) not united in the <s>Kula</s> [path] among the castes — they are said to grant liberation? Without the <s>Kaulika</s> [path], O Goddess, the divine eye does not [...]. (11.31) [...] of them, the lordship of <s>Kaula</s> would be great. Those incapable on the path of yoga should seek the <s>yoginī</s>. (11.32) [...lacuna...] for them there is no non-liberation. [...] one yoked in yoga to the <s>Kaulika</s> [path]. (11.33) Superior by birth and also by yoga — endowed with all sovereignty and excellent qualities.

body.translated_text: (12.2) Having properly consecrated the disciple, the <s>guru</s> should teach [the] entire supreme [knowledge] — the subtle and then the supreme; and afterward [should impart] realization [...]. (12.3) The gross is said to be of that nature [...lacuna...]. The supreme state of liberation is to be known — divine and auspicious, by the disciples. (12.4) For them, the <s>liṅga</s> is not of clay, not of stone, not of silver or gold, not a painted [...<s>liṅga</s>], [but in] one's own body [...]. (12.5) The <s>liṅga</s> to be worshipped in one's own body is the great abode of <s>dharma</s> and merit. [...] It is said [to grant both] enjoyment and liberation. (12.6) [...lacuna...] of the <s>yogin</s>s. It is to be worshipped above and below [...]. (12.7) [...lacuna...] it accomplishes liberation and wish-granting attainment. (12.8) The lord of <s>yoga</s>, as he desires [...lacuna...] attains liberation [...]. (12.9) There is no going elsewhere for him — this is the world's certainty. Thus, [all that is] situated within the egg of <s>Brahmā</s>, everything [...]. (12.10) [...] the partless [reality] — the <s>liṅga</s> of the <s>yogin</s>, presided over by the supreme <s>Śakti</s>. (12.11) The Self perceives directly [that which is] both with and without parts (<s>sakala-niṣkala</s>) [...], the abode of all deities. (12.12) Comprising all thirty-six [<s>tattva</s>s], the basis of all direct perception — he who sees the divine, O God, in the sky [...]. (12.13) [...] of clay and wood — the <s>liṅga</s> and image; [these are for] human <s>yogin</s>s; but one whose personal <s>liṅga</s> [is of the body] — (12.14) the <s>yogin</s> established in divine vision sees [...]. What need has he of image-forms, he who is established in divine attainment? (12.15) They see divine <s>liṅga</s>s, the supreme knowledge of the three worlds — what does an [external] <s>liṅga</s> do for one whose [vision is divine]? (12.16) He knows the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) situated in the body, born within the three worlds. This great glory of the <s>liṅga</s> — the lord of <s>yogin</s>s should always worship [it]. [A reflection ...] directly [...] the successive [levels of] yoga [...]. Without nectar, O Goddess, the lord of yogins [...]. Like a woman without shame [...] in a secluded, pleasant, secret place, one delights as one wishes [...] like a woman, the limbs [...] passionate [...] of one mutually enamored, the beloved produces the bliss of love. [...] attains <s>vairāgya</s> (detachment) [...] the <s>Kaulikī</s> [...] producing immediate realization [...] all [...]. Truly, truly, again [...]. Thus ends the twelfth chapter (<s>paṭala</s>) of the <s>Timirodghāṭana</s>.

body.translated_text: [The Trident of Knowledge (<s>Jñānaśūla</s>):] ...proclaimed. <s>Viṣṇu</s> is established in <s>kriyāśakti</s> (the power of action); <s>Umā</s> and <s>Soma</s> are proclaimed [in relation to it]. The power of will (<s>icchāśakti</s>)... <s>Śiva</s>... the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel)... is proclaimed as the <s>Vāmā</s> <s>Śakti</s>. And <s>Brāhmī</s> is the <s>Suṣumnā</s>, proclaimed as the <s>Jyeṣṭhā Śakti</s> (the eldest power). The middle one, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, is to be known [as...]. This trident of knowledge (<s>jñānaśūla</s>) is declared, endowed with the triad of <s>Śakti</s>s. Having pierced the <s>Soma</s> (moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (sun) and the third circle of fire (<s>agnimaṇḍala</s>), [it is] established in three lines... One should place [it] either in ashes or in water, with the trident of knowledge. He who worships <s>Svāyambhu Bhuvaneśvara</s> (the Self-born Lord of the World) in the midst of fire... the three worlds with [their] moving and unmoving [beings]... those who go [there] obtain that fruit. He who worships at the <s>Soma</s> pilgrimage site, the guardian of the self-born body — by that worship, all [is purified]... the formless (<s>niṣkala</s>)... the netherworld and the earth... at midday the moon rises. He who gives [a vessel] full of jewels, [practicing] the vow praised by yogins — [offering] flowers in one's own body... they obtain that fruit. In purity, one should arrange... the lord of the three worlds... [in the state of] dispassion... Having made a hymn of praise, and he who gives [a vessel] full of jewels to the teacher — [the merit is] tens of millions... in the body, in the <s>Śiva</s>-flower, twofold combined with fragrance, and fourfold by incense... by the obtainment of fragrance, flowers, and garlands... [the] heart... by the wish for the <s>mantra</s> syllables... that which is perfectly pure — the knower of <s>yoga</s> should unite the self there, together with the thread [of consciousness]... [reciting the] <s>mantra</s>... in the vital breaths, the <s>nāda</s> (inner sound) [resounds].

body.translated_text: The <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) spoke: That which is formless (<s>niṣkala</s>)... without stain (<s>nirmala</s>), peaceful (<s>śānta</s>), beyond phenomenal elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>), without characteristics, inconceivable, unknowable, devoid of destruction and origination, absolute isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>), solitary, peaceful, pure... the instrument, free from <s>yoga</s>, devoid of cause and means — from that, in an instant, they are liberated; tell me that knowledge, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>! Where there is <s>Śakti</s>, there is space (<s>ākāśa</s>) — [she is] situated in the body yet free from the body. How [is she] in the body? How is [she] free from the body? How does the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) abide in the body? What is the <s>jīva</s> called? By what does that <s>jīva</s> live? By what path does it travel? How is the <s>jīva</s> with parts (<s>sakala</s>), and how does it become partless (<s>niṣkala</s>)? How does that <s>jīva</s> see? What is the food of the <s>jīva</s>? Where does the <s>jīva</s> dissolve? And where indeed is it born? Of what color, of what measure is the <s>jīva</s>...? Tell me all of this, O God of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>! O Lord, [free me] from the bondage of the ocean of existence (<s>bhavasāgara</s>), the primal liberator!

The <s>Siddhakaulam</s> (perfected Kaula [teaching]) is renowned, free from downward movement; [...] and the fallen especially — one attains the state of being ageless and deathless, having arrived at the <s>cakra</s> (circle); [...] the authority of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, having resorted to <s>Akula</s> yoga, [...] a single footprint (seat) indeed. Likewise, the discerning one should always worship the Self; by which the ocean of <s>Kaula</s> (<s>Kaulārṇava</s>) has been declared — granting liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>. In every age, O Lord, [this teaching endures] until the end of the <s>Kaliyuga</s>; this divine <s>Kaula</s> [teaching] of his is never destroyed, by which all is always pervaded [...]. There is but one root, and its branches are many; by the power of that root, all that moves and is still sprouts forth. One seed, established in reality, resting in a single form, all-pervading like space, infinite, pure — the Lord. The cause at the end of the stainless, eternal in form, motionless, without self, not the various skies, by nature beyond conduct, devoid of the six colors, [fol. 45v] the reality unsupported [yet] hanging; in its own nature formless, in its own nature the middle of the body-aggregate. The yogin, eternally [manifest], should always perfect the supreme body-aggregate — united with a single <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), dwelling in a single place. There is no going to sacred seats (<s>pīṭhas</s>), nor offering grounds (<s>balikṣetras</s>); the <s>pīṭha</s> and <s>kṣetra</s> are established in the body — one does not wander to other sites. Where the supreme offering-fire is, there is the arising of <s>kula</s>. <s>Kula</s> is the support of <s>kula</s>, <s>kula</s> is the sacred seat (<s>pīṭha</s>), and <s>akula</s> is the guardian of the field. There is no assembly of <s>yoginīs</s> (<s>yoginīmelaka</s>), nor the sequence of ritual conduct; the great union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> — that is called the divine union (<s>divyamelā</s>). There is no meditation-yoga seat, no carrying of a yoga-staff, no shaving of hair, no girdle of <s>muñja</s> grass and the like, no loincloth, no vow, free from unmarked signs; no <s>saṃdhyā</s> (twilight worship), no fire-rites, no substances for <s>homa</s> (oblation) and the like. The great fire-pit is established in the body — a blazing circle of flame, resembling the fire of time (<s>kālānala</s>), equal in radiance to lightning; [...the lord of yoginīs...] the foundation of the world; attained without sequential stages, through the differentiation of <s>kula</s> [...]

body.translated_text: Or by effort, abandoning [all else], established in the state of single form; of all [...] like an ocean [...]. When the great path is seen, all reality [is known] without doubt. The reality established in a single form, situated in the pervader and the pervaded — this divine <s>Kaula</s> [teaching] is endowed with <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>. The <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Yoginīs</s>, established in all sacred seats (<s>pīṭhas</s>) — one should worship through the <s>kula</s> path, pervaded by the space-abiding [consciousness]. This divine [teaching] has been fully attained — that which is <s>kula</s>, the supreme seat. For him there are no <s>yantras</s> (diagrams) or <s>mantras</s>, no <s>nakṣatra</s>-mantra practices; he sees the equal savor (<s>samarasa</s>) — the verbal and the moving-and-still [world]. Having attained equanimity, free from passion, indifferent, with a peaceful mind, and that which has emerged from the mouth [of the guru], endowed with devotion to the <s>guru</s> — one should always observe the commitment (<s>samaya</s>), established in the state of single form. Then <s>ātmakaulam</s> (the Kaula of the Self) comes — one attains the state of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation). The yogin, by that [state], without desire, established in the state beyond conduct — he is liberated in all realities, liberated from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Having pervaded the state of agelessness and deathlessness, then liberation [comes] — there is no doubt. [fol. 47v] The yogin becomes a divine body-aggregate, free from wrinkles and grey hair; he wanders in the expanse of the sky, among gods, <s>Asuras</s>, and humans. He is never again bound by them — like a lotus petal by water. This is pure and divine, removing the darkness of bound souls (<s>paśus</s>). The <s>Siddhakaulam</s> (perfected Kaula) is to be known — it has been spoken by <s>Siddhanātha</s>. It does not abide between moon and sun, nor in fire and wind — it is to be reached through instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>), established in the mouth of the <s>guru</s>. Without conceptual thought, not grasped [by the mind], it has emerged from the blessed mouth [of the Lord] — infinite, pure, peaceful, devoid of marks of cause. This yoga has been declared by <s>Mīnanātha</s> — exceedingly rare to obtain.

body.translated_text: [Liberation is] not in the navel nor in the heart, not by the throat nor in the palate, not in the forehead, O beautiful one, nor at the tip of the uvula. Not through the flow of the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (cranial aperture), not in liberation, not in [mere] practice. Not in the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space above the head) — not in the mind's [...] nor in contemplation. Not by the mind's tracing of principles — neither liberation nor [attainment] exists [there]. Something may arise through the eye of intelligence, [but that is merely] the fabrication of intellect's bondage. [...lacuna...] O lovely one [...] exists.

body.translated_text: in the recitation [...]. [...] in the form of all principles — for them liberation does not exist. That which is the knot (<s>granthi</s>), O greatly fortunate one — [is] the form of knowledge, supreme and non-supreme. Having known the knot, O <s>Mahādevī</s>, [all] other knowledge [...]. The eyes, ears, nose, and mouth — having grasped [these with] the ever-auspicious [power], the divine channels (<s>nāḍī</s>), O Queen of Gods — having known [them], pervading [all] moving and unmoving [things]. Inhalation (<s>pūraka</s>), retention (<s>kumbhaka</s>), and exhalation (<s>recaka</s>), the third — one should abandon these, O Goddess, if one desires the supreme attainment! Now I shall fully declare the characteristic of the principle (<s>tattva</s>): neither conscious nor inert, neither self nor other; full, complete in the state of fullness, omniscient, bearing <s>Śrī</s> (glory); neither void nor perceptible, neither far nor in the middle; full, complete in the state of fullness, omniscient, bearing <s>Śrī</s>; neither in the body nor in the sky, nor in a state of wavering. Whatever is released from this — that state is declared the <s>Kaulika</s> realization.

children.translated_text: Having abandoned this [limited]
state, the state of fullness is the great bliss (<s>mahāsukha</s>).

children.text: bharitāvasthāmantrās tu & yo janāti sa kaulikaṃ
children.translated_text: He who knows the <s>mantra</s>s of the state of fullness — he [knows] the <s>Kaulika</s> [reality].
Gone to a single form, peaceful — [this is] the principle of the supreme and non-supreme.
